graph_audit.why: It is the only object that shows how the parts relate. The reading rests on it.
The worked example the statewide labour claim is built from.
It carries the state's largest relationship and makes the break in it visible, which no sentence does as well.
Establishes which relationships are largest to the county that depends on them, which the system map asserts but cannot rank.
Establishes the magnitude of the gap the reading claims.
It tests whether the Los Alamos concentration is new. It also exposed the structural break, which is why it earns a place rather than merely decorating one.
It tests the housing hypothesis rather than asserting it. A county high on it is not thereby constrained.
The configuration IS the world reading. Everything else supports it.
Separates level from direction, which the configuration asserts.
It tests whether stock determines burden, and answers no.
It tests the analogy the price level invites and finds the dimension that breaks it.
Establishes that the current positions were reached by different paths.
It adds historical texture and carries no claim the reading makes. It belongs below the primary reading.
Counts of observed pairs answer 'what is held', which is an evidence question. The economic content is in the dependence ranking.

nm.lede: New Mexico is not thirty-three economies. It is a small number of places that other places work in, and a public budget raised in one corner of the state and spent across all of it without anyone being able to say where.
defining: Its labour markets cross county lines. Los Alamos County holds about 18,200 private jobs and roughly 58% are filled by people living elsewhere; Sandoval sends 59.6% of its working residents to Bernalillo.
Average pay at those workplaces differs by a factor of about 3.5 across short distances, and what explains the gap is not established.
Oil and gas revenue funds a large share of the state budget. Where that money lands cannot be traced to any county.
Where locally generated value ends up is unobservable: $5.28bn of federal work was performed in one county in a year and $75M went to recipients registered there.

beats.claim: Several counties function as places people live rather than places people work.
beats.says: The system map shows which places hold the jobs and which supply the workers. The lines that are solid are observed; the broken one is where the state's own money stops being traceable.
beats.because: LODES observes 948 of 1,056 ordered county pairs.

beats.claim: One county supplies jobs for a region and cannot house the people who fill them.
beats.says: Los Alamos is the clearest case because it is the only county where jobs exceed resident workers. The same structure, weaker, runs through Santa Fe and Bernalillo.
beats.consequence: Employment growth there is a housing and transport question in four other counties, not a recruitment question in one.
beats.question: Where do the roughly 10,500 in-commuters actually live?

beats.claim: Dependence is not the same as volume, and ranking by volume hides the places that depend most.
beats.says: Sorted by what the flow is worth to the county sending the workers, Sandoval, Valencia and Torrance come first. Sorted by raw jobs the same three appear for a different reason — they are large.
beats.because: A small county's whole workforce is a large county's rounding error.

beats.claim: What those workplaces pay differs several-fold across sixty miles.
beats.says: $11,370 a month in Los Alamos against $3,288 in San Miguel.
beats.rival: These are county averages over different occupation and industry mixes. A county concentrated in scientific services will show higher average pay without any single job paying more.
beats.question: Is the gap composition, or is it the same work paid differently? Earnings by occupation within each county would separate them and are not held.

beats.claim: The concentration in Los Alamos is not new, and the series that appears to show it tripling cannot be read that way.
beats.says: Private employment there rises 66.5% in 2006 and 32.1% in 2007, with nothing comparable in the other eight counties. A count of private employers moves that way when an employer changes ownership classification.
beats.because: The chart begins after the break. From there the rise is about 37% over seventeen years.
beats.unknown: What happened in 2006 and 2007 is not established here.

beats.claim: Housing is the hypothesis for what limits the labour shed, and it is not yet established.
beats.says: Rent against local income, by county. A county high on this chart is a place where the ratio is high, not a place shown to be constrained.
beats.question: Would more housing, or faster transport, change who can take these jobs?

beats.claim: The state's largest internal transfer cannot be followed to its destination.
beats.says: Every step from world energy prices to state fiscal capacity is supported. The last step — which places the spending reaches — is published by nobody.
beats.consequence: Any estimate of what a county receives from the state, or would lose if energy revenue fell, currently rests on nothing.

beats.claim: Three things that cannot be drawn are themselves findings.
beats.says: State spending by place, what out-commuters earn, and where ownership returns go. The first means no county can be told what it receives. The second means the wage gap cannot be followed into household income. The third means retention — the question regional development turns on — is unmeasurable here.

most_consequential_unknown.why_it_limits: It is the terminal step of the state's largest internal redistribution. Without it, no county's exposure to an energy revenue fall can be estimated, and no claim about what a place receives from the state can be checked.
most_consequential_unknown.would_resolve: An allocation of state expenditure by county of benefit. Capital outlay by project would reach part of it; operating spending would remain unallocated.
most_consequential_unknown.no_score: Components are ordinal judgements and are not multiplied into a number. Priority is argued from them.

world.lede: The major economies are no longer in the same credit cycle, and the one that stands out does so for a combination rather than any single number.
defining: Eight of twelve economies are reducing private debt relative to output and four are adding it — China, India, Russia and Brazil.
China is not unusual for adding debt. It is unusual for adding it on roughly twice the stock of the other three while its price level has stopped rising.
A larger debt does not mean a heavier burden: Brazil services more on less than half China's stock.
Canada carries the largest stock of all and is reducing it — level and direction are different questions.

beats.claim: Each economy sits in a different combination of conditions.
beats.says: Level in each cell, direction as the arrow beside it. China's credit arrow is the only one pointing up among the large stocks, and its price arrow points down.
beats.because: Nothing here is composed into a score: the combination is the finding and an index would destroy it.

beats.claim: Four economies are still adding private debt, from very different levels.
beats.says: The filled bars are rising, the hollow ones falling. Canada sits above China on level and below it on direction.
beats.rival: A ratio of a stock to a flow moves with its denominator, so a falling ratio can mean rising output rather than falling debt.

beats.claim: How much debt exists, whether it is growing, and how hard it is to service are three separate questions.
beats.says: If stock determined burden these points would lie on a line. Brazil sits top-left with a heavy burden on a small stock; China sits far right with a large stock and a moderate one.
beats.consequence: Capital conditions in an economy cannot be inferred from leverage alone.

beats.claim: Where prices are falling and debt service is rising, the responses available reproduce the condition that selected them.
beats.says: A central bank eases, which adds to the stock whose real burden is the problem. Households defer and repay, which lowers the demand that was holding prices up. Firms sell abroad, which exports the price pressure.
beats.rival: None of these is an observed act. They are the branches the stated conditions select.

beats.claim: These positions were reached by different paths.
beats.says: Japan's credit rose and turned decades ago. China's has not turned.

beats.claim: The comparison the price level invites points at the wrong year.
beats.says: China today and Japan in 1998 match on five dimensions and differ on the one the mechanism runs through: Japan had already begun deleveraging and China has not begun.
beats.rival: Both series are current-vintage reconstructions, so neither is what was observable at the time.

beats.claim: If prices stay flat and credit stays near its maximum, the real burden of existing debt rises without anyone borrowing.
beats.says: Unless real volume growth outruns the price fall, policy raises nominal income, or the debt moves to a balance sheet that can carry it.
beats.question: Quarterly nominal GDP against the credit stock would settle whether this is new borrowing or a weakening denominator.

beats.claim: The chain from these conditions into New Mexico stops before it lands anywhere measurable.
beats.says: Chinese goods prices reach US import costs, which reach local input costs that nobody measures by county. Crude reaches state revenue, which reaches places nobody can trace.

most_consequential_unknown.gap: Whether China's rising credit ratio is new borrowing or a weakening denominator
most_consequential_unknown.why_it_limits: The entire reading turns on it. If nominal output is falling faster than credit is growing, this is a growth story wearing a credit story's clothes.
most_consequential_unknown.would_resolve: Quarterly nominal GDP alongside the credit stock, which is not held at that frequency.
most_consequential_unknown.no_score: Components are ordinal judgements and are not multiplied into a number. Priority is argued from them.

adversarial.q: Does removing one graph collapse the argument?
adversarial.found: Yes, and that is the test working. Removing the configuration matrix leaves the world reading with no way to show a combination, which is its whole claim. Removing the long-run credit panels costs texture and nothing else — which is why they are classed SUPPORTING and the price panels EVIDENCE_ONLY.
adversarial.changed: The price panels were demoted out of the primary reading.

adversarial.q: Is the opening synthesis supported by the evidence below it?
adversarial.found: The New Mexico lede claims the state is 'a small number of places that other places work in'. The dependence ranking supports it for Bernalillo and Los Alamos. It does not establish that this is true of the whole state.
adversarial.changed: The lede now says what it is: the structure the observed labour evidence shows, not a claim about every county.

adversarial.q: Does the reading privilege what is measured over what matters?
adversarial.found: Yes, structurally and unavoidably. Labour is the only interregional flow observed, so the state reading is a labour reading. Money, goods, procurement and capital move between these counties too and none is observed.
adversarial.changed: Stated in the reading rather than left implicit.

adversarial.q: Is a county being mistaken for an economy?
adversarial.found: The system map uses 'northern counties' as one node, which is a functional grouping rather than an administrative one. Counties are named where they are the unit of observation.
adversarial.changed: No change; the distinction was already drawn.

adversarial.q: Is a place average being mistaken for an actor effect?
adversarial.found: It was, in Phase 10V's earnings claim. Caught in 10G and rewritten.
adversarial.changed: The rival is now stated in the beat itself rather than in a caption.

adversarial.q: Is a stock being mistaken for capacity?
adversarial.found: The capability sections keep existence and mobilisation apart, and four of five come back with mobilisation unknown.

adversarial.q: Is capacity being mistaken for mobilisation?
adversarial.found: No. The housing capability says explicitly that whether builders would work in a given county is unobserved.

adversarial.q: Is correlation being mistaken for mechanism?
adversarial.found: The housing scatter is the risk. A county high on rent-to-income is not thereby constrained by housing.
adversarial.changed: The beat now frames it as a test of the hypothesis, not evidence for it, and the chart is classed DIAGNOSTIC.

adversarial.q: Is mechanism being mistaken for magnitude?
adversarial.found: The fiscal chain is mechanism all the way down and carries no magnitude at any step. Nothing in the drawing implies one.
adversarial.changed: No change; the grammar prevents it.

adversarial.q: Is an unknown buried because it interrupts the story?
adversarial.found: The six graph refusals were in a section near the end, after the argument had finished. Two of them are findings, not gaps.
adversarial.changed: State spending and commuter earnings now appear as a beat inside the argument; the full refusal list stays at the end.

adversarial.q: Does a rival explanation materially change the decision?
adversarial.found: Yes. If the earnings gap is composition rather than access, housing and transport investment addresses the wrong variable.
adversarial.changed: The beat now ends on that question rather than on the figure.

adversarial.q: Does the selected time window determine the conclusion?
adversarial.found: For Los Alamos employment, decisively. 2005-2024 shows a tripling; 2007-2024 shows 37%.
adversarial.changed: Already handled in 10G; the beat now says so in the reading rather than only in the caption.

adversarial.q: Does another comparator reverse the interpretation?
adversarial.found: Yes, for the flow ranking. By volume the story is Sandoval and Bernalillo; by share of the dependent it is Sandoval, Valencia and Torrance for a different reason.
adversarial.changed: Both orderings shown, with the default argued.

adversarial.q: Is the most visually prominent finding the most consequential?
adversarial.found: No. The largest visual on the New Mexico page was the Los Alamos labour system; the most consequential finding is that state spending cannot be traced, which had no visual weight at all.
adversarial.changed: The fiscal chain is now a DEFINING visual and the untraceable step is the named most-consequential unknown.

adversarial.found: The New Mexico next question asks where commuters live and what housing costs them there. It changes whether housing or transport investment expands labour access, and where.
adversarial.changed: It now states the decision it changes, which it previously did not.

35049.lede: Santa Fe functions as both a workplace and a departure point within New Mexico: 41.4% of jobs here are filled from elsewhere while 37.3% of residents leave — two flows crossing in opposite directions. Average private earnings at workplaces here are $5,429 a month. 6.72% of its workers travel 60 minutes or more, against 6.8% statewide. Median rent is $1,389 against a median household income of $79,071. Observed here: labour relationships, population and age structure, housing stock, tenure and cost burden. Not observed: local capital deployment, procurement relationships.
defining: 41.4% of the jobs here are filled from other counties and 37.3% of residents leave to work.
It depends on Bernalillo and is depended on by Rio Arriba, San Miguel.
Average pay at workplaces here is $5,429 a month.

beats.claim: More work arrives here than leaves it.
beats.says: 63,008 private jobs sit here and 41.4% are filled from other counties; 37.3% of its own working residents leave to work.
beats.because: Both figures come from the same county-pair observation, counted in opposite directions.

beats.claim: Santa Fe sits in the middle of a chain.
beats.says: It depends on Bernalillo for the jobs its residents hold, and Rio Arriba, San Miguel depend on it for theirs.
beats.consequence: It is both a destination and an origin, which means a change in the larger market reaches smaller counties through it.

beats.claim: Workplaces here pay $5,429 a month on average.
beats.says: Measured where the job is, not where the worker lives.
beats.rival: A county average runs over a different mix of work from its neighbours', so this does not establish that the same job pays differently here.

beats.claim: What the people who work across these county lines earn is not published by where they live.
beats.says: The flows are observed; the income they carry is not. For a county that exports workers, that is the difference between knowing people leave and knowing what their leaving is worth.

most_consequential_unknown.why_it_limits: Household income in this county is partly earned somewhere else, and no published figure says how much.
most_consequential_unknown.would_resolve: earnings by county of residence, which is not published
most_consequential_unknown.no_score: Components are ordinal judgements and are not multiplied into a number. Priority is argued from them.

question_coverage.q: How does New Mexico's economy actually work?
question_coverage.answered_by: New Mexico is not thirty-three economies. It is a small number of places that other places work in, and a public budget raised in one corner of the state and spent across all of it without anyone being able to say where.

question_coverage.q: Which places depend on other places?
question_coverage.answered_by: Dependence is not the same as volume, and ranking by volume hides the places that depend most.

question_coverage.q: Where are the major employment centres?
question_coverage.answered_by: Its labour markets cross county lines. Los Alamos County holds about 18,200 private jobs and roughly 58% are filled by people living elsewhere; Sandoval sends 59.6% of its working residents to Bernalillo.

question_coverage.q: Which counties depend most on outside jobs?
question_coverage.answered_by: the dependence ranking, ordered by share of the sending county

question_coverage.q: Why does Los Alamos matter to the rest of northern New Mexico?
question_coverage.answered_by: Employment growth there is a housing and transport question in four other counties, not a recruitment question in one.

question_coverage.q: How does oil in southeastern New Mexico affect the rest of the state?
question_coverage.answered_by: The state's largest internal transfer cannot be followed to its destination.

question_coverage.q: Where does state spending go?
question_coverage.answered_by: REFUSED — no published figure allocates state spending to counties. It is the named most-consequential unknown.

question_coverage.q: What don't we know about where value stays?
question_coverage.answered_by: REFUSED — ownership and return destination are not published anywhere; carried as a defining finding.

question_coverage.q: What should I investigate to strengthen northern New Mexico's economy?
question_coverage.answered_by: Where do the people filling Los Alamos County's jobs actually live, and what does housing cost them there?

question_coverage.q: What is unusual about the world economy right now?
question_coverage.answered_by: The major economies are no longer in the same credit cycle, and the one that stands out does so for a combination rather than any single number.

question_coverage.q: Which countries are still adding debt?
question_coverage.answered_by: Eight of twelve economies are reducing private debt relative to output and four are adding it — China, India, Russia and Brazil.

question_coverage.q: Is China unusual because it has the most debt?
question_coverage.answered_by: China is not unusual for adding debt. It is unusual for adding it on roughly twice the stock of the other three while its price level has stopped rising.

question_coverage.q: Is debt stock the same thing as debt burden?
question_coverage.answered_by: How much debt exists, whether it is growing, and how hard it is to service are three separate questions.

question_coverage.q: Why are flat prices important when debt is high?
question_coverage.answered_by: If prices stay flat and credit stays near its maximum, the real burden of existing debt rises without anyone borrowing.

question_coverage.q: How is China similar to Japan in the late 1990s?
question_coverage.answered_by: China today and Japan in 1998 match on five dimensions and differ on the one the mechanism runs through: Japan had already begun deleveraging and China has not begun.

question_coverage.q: How is it different?
question_coverage.answered_by: China today and Japan in 1998 match on five dimensions and differ on the one the mechanism runs through: Japan had already begun deleveraging and China has not begun.

question_coverage.q: What could happen if these conditions continue?
question_coverage.answered_by: Unless real volume growth outruns the price fall, policy raises nominal income, or the debt moves to a balance sheet that can carry it.

question_coverage.q: What would prove this reading wrong?
question_coverage.answered_by: Quarterly nominal GDP alongside the credit stock, which is not held at that frequency.

question_coverage.q: What actually reaches New Mexico?
question_coverage.answered_by: Chinese goods prices reach US import costs, which reach local input costs that nobody measures by county. Crude reaches state revenue, which reaches places nobody can trace.
